THIS WEEK IN LOCAL GOVERNMENT

Wausau city leaders committed roughly $4.5 million to replace private-side lead service lines and opened 2027 budget season, while Marathon County moved a nearly $55 million highway facility expansion toward a full board vote.

  • The Wausau City Council voted to cover an estimated $4.5 million gap for private-side lead service line replacements in 2027, choosing full city funding under Option C.
  • The council also rezoned Honey Locust Court properties (7100–7123) from SR2 to DR8 for twin-home development, passing over the district alder's objections.
  • Marathon County supervisors reviewed a $54.98 million resolution for phase four of a new county highway facility at an educational session; the HR Finance & Property Committee and full board are set to vote October 20.
  • The Wausau Finance Committee set pet license fees for 2027 — $25 for spayed/neutered animals with a $10 microchip discount — and scheduled a final budget workshop for October 20.
  • Marathon County's HR, Finance & Property Committee unanimously authorized publication of the proposed 2027 budget, which carries a $66.25 million levy and a mill rate of 3.4773, with a public hearing set for November 2.
  • Kronenwetter's Administrative Policy Committee recommended closing municipal center offices to walk-in traffic Friday afternoons and adopting a written public comment procedure with a Wednesday submission deadline.

Coming up: Monday, Kronenwetter kicks off its first 2027 budget workshop at 3 p.m. and its Plan Commission meets at 6 p.m. to consider a conditional use permit for a nonmetallic mine, a rezoning request, and a land division. Tuesday, Marathon County's HR Finance & Property Committee takes up the $54.98 million highway facility resolution at 3 p.m., followed by the full County Board that evening, and Wausau's Finance Committee holds its final 2027 budget workshop at 6:30 p.m.
